title: When wages cannot fall

controls.label: Fall in labour demand (thousands at each wage)

predict.q: A regional labour market is in equilibrium at a wage of 10 and 600 thousand workers. A minimum wage of 10 is in place. Then demand for labour falls by 160 thousand at each wage. What happens?

options.s: The wage stays at 10; employment falls to 440 thousand; 160 thousand are unemployed
options.fb: The floor stops the wage falling: firms hire only 440 thousand while 600 thousand want work at 10.

options.s: The wage falls to 8; employment falls to 520 thousand; 80 thousand are unemployed
options.fb: That is what happens if the wage can fall: it drops to 8 and the market clears. With a floor at 10 the wage cannot fall, so firms hire only 440 thousand and 600 thousand still want work.

options.s: Employment stays at 600 thousand, because the wage cannot change
options.fb: A fixed wage does not fix jobs. Firms hire where the wage meets the new, lower demand curve: 440 thousand.

options.s: Labour supply falls by 160 thousand too, so no unemployment appears
options.fb: Demand for labour fell, not supply. At a wage of 10, 600 thousand still want to work, so 160 thousand are unemployed.

task: Move the fall-in-demand slider and the minimum-wage slider and watch the wage, employment and the gap between labour supplied and labour demanded.

target.do: Move the fall-in-demand slider to 160 (minimum wage 10), then press Check.

takeaway: When wages cannot fall, a fall in labour demand shows up as unemployment, not as lower pay.
explore: Set the minimum wage to 6 with a fall of 160: the wage falls to 8 and 520 thousand work, with no unemployment at the going wage.
